codes.target: duende as a marker of true flamenco sound
codes.rationale: The passage defines duende as an ultimate flamenco moment tied to the transmission of true sound, giving it authenticity value.

codes.evidence_quote: The following three questions shall be the point of this discussion: 1. Who is allowed to have "duende"? 2. Is the "duende" that is transmitted equal to the "duende" received?
codes.rationale: The article explicitly treats duende as a criterion to be defined, transmitted, received, and debated in flamenco performance.

codes.evidence_quote: But to answer the question, it is the second type that is allowed to have "duende".

derived_analysis.target: duende and those authorized to have it

annotation_notes: The author frames the definition as provisional, but still answers who is allowed to have duende.

codes.evidence_quote: we cannot bring about any type of direct investigation to gauge what is true and what is false in those examples.
codes.target: attributed flamenco styles of long-gone cantaores
codes.rationale: The passage explicitly questions the truth or falsity of inherited attributions and the authenticity of personal creations.

codes.evidence_quote: Each cantaor interprets, in his way, the flamenco legacy; without expressive personality, everything would be converted into a mummified replica.
codes.target: flamenco legacy and continuity through interpretation
codes.rationale: The passage grounds present flamenco value in inherited legacy while insisting that continuity requires living reinterpretation rather than frozen replication.

codes.evidence_quote: The styles which are attributed to cantaores long-gone had, necessarily, to reach us by way of those who reproduced in their own way the characteristics of those primitive cantaores.
codes.target: transmission of flamenco styles across singers
codes.rationale: The passage describes oral/lineage transmission through reproduction and adaptation by later cantaores as the route by which older styles survive.

codes.evidence_quote: the great cantaores whose fame has reached us today... The first useful recordings -- the immediate proof -- is possible only in the era of Manuel Torre, Chacón, Juan Breva, El Tenazas, El Gloria. Before them, everything is supposition.
codes.rationale: The article constructs a hierarchy of historical authority by distinguishing famous great cantaores and treating early recordings as the first reliable proof.
